Indoor window treatments

Motorized Shades in Palm Beach County

Raise and lower shades with a remote, an app, or a schedule. Especially useful on tall glass, wide sliders, and windows you can't easily reach.

Get a Free Consultation Call 561-332-8091

We bring samples to your home so you can compare options at your own windows.

Is it a fit?

Where motorized shades work well

  • Tall, wide, or hard-to-reach windows
  • Rooms where the sun moves across the day, using schedules
  • Homes with young children or pets, since there are no cords
  • Seasonal residents who want to control shades from anywhere through a connected hub
Ask about motorized shades

Good to know before you choose

Power
Rechargeable battery motors usually install without new wiring. Hardwired motors fit best in new construction or a remodel.
Smart-home control
We install Hunter Douglas PowerView, Somfy, and comparable motors. Many work with Alexa, Google Home, and Apple HomeKit through a hub. We confirm compatibility with your setup before you order.
Fabric still matters
Motorization changes how the shade moves, not how much light or privacy it gives. That comes from the fabric you choose.
How it works

Three steps to finished motorized shades

  1. Consultation at your home

    We bring samples, look at your windows in real light, and talk through what you need.

  2. Measurement and a written proposal

    Each opening is measured, and you get the products, options, and price in writing.

  3. Installation and walkthrough

    Our own installers fit, adjust, and explain everything before they leave.

Questions

Motorized Shades questions

Do I need an electrician?

Often not. Battery-powered motors usually install without new wiring. If you're building or remodeling, a hardwired setup may make more sense, and we'll recommend based on your windows.

Can I add motors to shades later?

Sometimes, but many shades can't be converted. If you think you'll want motorization, mention it at the consultation so the right hardware is chosen up front.

What decides the price?

The number and size of shades, the fabric, the motor and power type, and whether you add a hub or sensors. Your written proposal breaks it down so you can compare options.
